text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to meet on Thursday at Erez crossing.
- Palestinian Legislative Council speaker Ahmed Korei: Palestinian Authority to build legislative council building in Al-Bireh beside Ramallah.
- Hebron's Shuhada Street to be partially opened to Palestinians today.
- Government fails to achieve budget surplus in January. Treasury director-general David Brodet: 1997 growth may fall short of 4 percent target.
- Bank workers plan Friday strikes in unilateral attempt to move to a five-day work week.
- Bank Hapoalim issuing long-term promissory notes -- capital notes similar to bonds -- in attempt to raise $200 million abroad.
- Super-Sol merger with Shekem approved by the Antitrust Authority.
- Palestinian Authority promises response to Israeli debt demand.
HAARETZ

- Prime minister intervened in dispute between Finance Minister Dan Meridor and Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel on the exchange rate policy. Governor backs change in policy; Meridor conditions it on lowering of the interest rate.
- Housing ministry proposal: 50 million shekels to be cut from the mortgages of the needy for the benefit of the Jewish settlements.
- Class size in Arab sector on average -- the highest.
- Rabbi Eliezer Schach, leader of Degel Hatorah party, is hospitalised in Ichilov medical centre intensive care.
- Prime minister: "I heard from President Mubarak very interesting things in the Syrian matter". Arafat, in his speech in Davos, bitterly attacks Israeli government.
MAARIV
- Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak to Maariv: I'll work to strengthen economic ties with Israel.
- Israel's Foreign Minister David Levy: Syria has awful chemical weaponry.
- Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani: "Israeli soldiers are like sitting ducks in Lebanon".
- Probe into attorney-general scandal advances only on the "second level".
- F-22 the plane the United States is offering Israel.
- Stock exchange responds positively to Davos summit -- shares up 2.7 percent.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- 30 Iranian planes brought Hizbollah weaponry into Syria, Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy says.
- Discussions in Davos, Switzerland, on Israeli exchange rate between Israeli leaders and two American economists.
